description: Text tools: grep, diff, sed, jq, patch and cmp edge cases.

cases.name: text-tools: jq del multi-index descending order
text-tools: jq del object keys
text-tools: jq del nested paths
text-tools: jq scan ignores caller flags for globalness
text-tools: diff DIR FILE without -r
cases.script: mkdir dz; echo content >dz/f1; echo content2 >f1; diff dz f1; echo status=$?

cases.name: text-tools: diff FILE DIR without -r
cases.script: mkdir dz; echo content >dz/f1; echo content2 >f1; diff f1 dz; echo status=$?

cases.name: text-tools: diff DIR1 DIR2 without -r stays at the top level
cases.script: mkdir -p d1/sub d2/sub; echo a >d1/x; echo b >d2/x; echo c >d1/only1; echo same >d1/sub/y; echo same >d2/sub/y; diff d1 d2; echo status=$?

cases.name: text-tools: patch .rej header uses the stripped name
cases.script:
mkdir -p a b; printf 'AAA
BBB
CCC
' >x.txt; printf -- '--- a/x.txt
+++ b/x.txt
@@ -1,3 +1,3 @@
 one
-two
+TWO
 three
' >p.diff; patch -p1 x.txt p.diff; echo status=$?; cat x.txt.rej

cases.name: text-tools: patch -R on a not-yet-applied patch says Unreversed
cases.script:
printf 'one
two
three
' >x.txt; printf -- '--- x.txt
+++ x.txt
@@ -1,3 +1,3 @@
 one
-two
+TWO
 three
' >p.diff; patch -R x.txt p.diff; echo status=$?; cat x.txt.rej

cases.name: text-tools: patch backs up on offset but not on an exact match
cases.script:
printf 'one
two
three
' >f; printf -- '--- f
+++ f
@@ -1,3 +1,3 @@
 one
-two
+TWO
 three
' >p.diff; patch f p.diff; echo status=$?; ls f.orig 2>/dev/null; echo none=$?; printf '0
0
0
0
0
line1
line2
line3
' >g; printf -- '--- g
+++ g
@@ -1,3 +1,3 @@
 line1
-line2
+LINE2
 line3
' >p2.diff; patch g p2.diff; echo status=$?; cat g.orig

cases.name: text-tools: patch --dry-run omits the saving-rejects suffix
cases.script:
printf 'AAA
BBB
CCC
' >x.txt; printf -- '--- x.txt
+++ x.txt
@@ -1,3 +1,3 @@
 one
-two
+TWO
 three
' >p.diff; patch --dry-run x.txt p.diff; echo status=$?; ls x.txt.rej 2>/dev/null; echo none=$?

cases.name: text-tools: diff -d is a real accepted no-op
text-tools: diff -e lists multiple change hunks from the end of the file backwards
text-tools: diff -e's later hunk keeps the original file's line numbers after an earlier delete
text-tools: diff -e's later hunk keeps the original file's line numbers after an earlier insert
text-tools: diff -e mixes a, c and d commands in one script, still bottom-up
text-tools: diff -e of byte-identical files missing a trailing newline still warns
cases.script:
printf '1
2
3' >eo5; printf '1
2
3' >en5; diff -e eo5 en5; echo status=$?

cases.name: text-tools: diff -e escapes a lone . line in an append
text-tools: diff -e escapes a lone . line in a change
text-tools: diff -e escapes several . lines in the same hunk
cases.script:
printf '1
2
' >edo3; printf '1
.
.
' >edn3; diff -e edo3 edn3; rm -f edo3 edn3

cases.name: text-tools: diff -e escapes a . line at the very end of a hunk
text-tools: diff -e escapes a . line with content on both sides of it
text-tools: cmp -b prints differing bytes
cases.script: printf a >f1; printf b >f2; cmp -b f1 f2

cases.name: text-tools: patch -f is refused not misread

expected.reason: diff/cmp/patch options bash-tool refuses rather than implements

cases.name: text-tools: jq division by an exact-zero divisor raises jq's own error
text-tools: jq remainder by an exact-zero divisor raises jq's own error
text-tools: jq indexing an object by a non-string key raises jq's own error
text-tools: jq nan and infinite still work as native constants
text-tools: grep -r with one plain file operand omits the filename prefix
text-tools: grep -r with one directory operand keeps the filename prefix
cases.script: mkdir d; printf 'one\n' > d/nums; grep -rn one d

cases.name: text-tools: grep -m0 selects nothing
cases.script: printf 'one\ntwo\n' > f; grep -m0 one f; echo status=$?

cases.name: text-tools: grep -A0 still separates non-adjacent matches
cases.script:
printf 'one
two
three
four
five
six
' > f; grep -A0 -e two -e six f

cases.name: text-tools: grep -z lets . match an embedded newline
text-tools: grep -P \d is ASCII-only
text-tools: grep --include filters an explicit file operand
cases.script: printf 'one\n' > nums.txt; grep --include='*.log' one nums.txt; echo status=$?

cases.name: text-tools: grep --exclude-dir filters a directory operand itself
cases.script: mkdir sub; printf 'one\n' > sub/f; grep -r --exclude-dir=sub one sub; echo status=$?

cases.name: text-tools: grep -f pattern file with a raw non-UTF-8 byte matches that byte
text-tools: jq replaces invalid UTF-8 input with U+FFFD on output
text-tools: sed \xff in a script matches and produces a raw byte
text-tools: sed \xff matches a raw byte in ERE mode too
text-tools: sed y/// with a \xff byte escape matches a raw byte
text-tools: sed \xff does not match a real multi-byte UTF-8 character
text-tools: sed matches a raw byte from a shell variable, not just \xff syntax
text-tools: sed -i matches a raw byte from a shell variable too
cases.script: x=$'\xff'; printf '\xff\n' > gc072; sed -i "s/$x/X/" gc072; od -An -tx1 gc072

cases.name: text-tools: grep -f - reads patterns from the shell's stdin
text-tools: grep -E -F together is refused as conflicting
text-tools: grep -G -G repeated is fine
cases.script: echo a | grep -G -G a; echo status=$?

cases.name: text-tools: grep -- group separator appears between file operands, not just within one
cases.script:
printf 'a
match
b
' > gsep1; grep -C1 match gsep1 gsep1

cases.name: text-tools: grep -E a{,2} treats a missing lower bound as 0
text-tools: grep BRE a\{,2\} treats a missing lower bound as 0
text-tools: grep BRE a leading \{1\} is literal text

expected.reason: Matches GNU byte for byte on stdout; GNU's own stderr warning ('stray \ before {') isn't reproduced, since it doesn't affect matching or status and grep's basic()/extended() translators have no way to emit one.

cases.name: text-tools: grep -E a leading {1} is dropped, not literal

expected.reason: Matches GNU byte for byte on stdout; GNU's own stderr warning ('{...} at start of expression') isn't reproduced, for the same reason as the BRE case above.

cases.name: text-tools: sed compile error names the -e expression, not a raw location
text-tools: grep --color=always highlights matches with GNU's SGR sequences
text-tools: grep --color=always colors the filename, line number and separator
text-tools: grep --color=always with -o colors just the matched text
text-tools: grep --color=always colors matches on context lines and the -- separator
text-tools: grep -v with --color=always produces no color
text-tools: grep --color=auto produces no color when stdout is not a terminal
text-tools: grep --color (bare, defaults to auto) produces no color
text-tools: grep --color=never produces no color
text-tools: sed -i continues past an unreadable file
cases.script: printf 'a\n' >fa082; sed -i 's/a/z/' nope082 fa082; echo s=$?; cat fa082

cases.name: text-tools: sed e command refuses with the README's exact wording

stderr.text: sed: the 'e' command and substitute flag are unsupported in bash-tool: no shell to run

expected.reason: GNU actually runs `date`; this build has no shell to run it, and refuses with the wording/status the README documents for that.

cases.name: text-tools: jq zero-step range yields nothing instead of hanging
text-tools: jq moderate string repeat still works
text-tools: jq excessive string repeat refuses instead of aborting
text-tools: sed --help respects stdout redirection instead of leaking to real stdio
text-tools: sed -@ respects stderr redirection instead of leaking to real stdio
text-tools: sed --version reports its own name after another uucore tool has run
cases.script: wc --version >/dev/null; sed --version | head -1 | cut -d' ' -f1; echo status=$?
